title: Cart lab: change mass
target: Use a controlled comparison to describe the effect of system mass on acceleration.
criteria: Identify total moving mass and keep driving force fixed.
Compare acceleration values using a fair test.
Separate model data from measured evidence.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: In a connected cart-and-hanger experiment, which mass determines acceleration for the complete moving system?
options: Only the mass of the table.
Only the cart’s empty mass in every setup.
The total moving mass of cart, hanger, and carried loads.
Only the hanging mass in every setup.
cpa.guide: The chosen system includes all masses that accelerate together.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: To test acceleration versus total mass fairly, which quantity must be held fixed?
cpa.guide: Mass is the varied quantity; hold net force constant.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A fixed 12 N net force accelerates a 3 kg system. What acceleration is predicted?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: At unchanged net force, a system’s mass triples. How does its acceleration change?
cpa.guide: a ∝ 1/m when net force is fixed.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A worksheet supplies mass and acceleration values. What can a student legitimately report from analyzing them?
options: A measurement uncertainty of exactly zero.
A relationship supported by the supplied example data.
Proof that all real friction is zero.
A claim that they personally measured every value.
cpa.guide: Analyzing model data does not substitute for performing a measurement.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A measured trial disagrees with F_net/m using hanger weight as F_net. Which check is useful?
options: Whether resistance was omitted and whether the chosen system includes the hanger.
Assume hanger weight always equals tension and net cart force.
Change the reported acceleration to fit.
cpa.guide: Hanger weight, tension, and net cart force are distinct; choose the system consistently.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
